summary: Working in history and archaeology, Isaac Schapera studied at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town (~1921–1925), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1929). He held posts at Chicago (~1948), Toronto, and LSE (~1950–1969), and taught Bridget Allchin.

A scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, Schmidt earned a doctorate at Rostock. He held posts at the Russian Bible Society (1812–1824), Saint Petersburg State University (~1842–1847), and the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1829–1847).

Specializing in Tibetology, Henrion-Dourcy studied at Université libre de Bruxelles (~1990–2004), EPHE, Harvard, and Tibet University, working under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).
Isabelle Onians, who works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 2002. She was an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library (attested 2007).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Ratié studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Alexis Sanderson and Lyne Bansat-Boudon. Her posts include Leipzig (~2009–2012), Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

Isaiah Berlin worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. After studying at St Paul's School (~1922–1928) and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932), he held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1975.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Horner studied under Caroline Rhys Davids and at Newnham College and Cambridge. She held positions at Newnham College, Cambridge's Governing Body (1939–1949), and the Pali Text Society (1942, 1959–1981).
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. By 1976, he held posts as professor at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Active in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Isao Nishitani held a post at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and served as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Working in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Iselin Frydenlund held posts as a research fellow at the University of Oslo and as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo (both attested 2016).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Vidyasagar studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Sanskrit College. He held posts at Fort William College (1841–1846, 1849), Sanskrit College (1846–1849), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

Specializing in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies, Kern studied at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University. He held posts at KU Leuven (1962–1971), Heidelberg (~1973–1979), Bern (1985), Zurich (~1985–2002), and Fribourg (~1985–2002).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Issaien Ikeyama held positions as professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College (attested 1976).
Issei Suzuki worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University and later held a post as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Sophia University and earned a master's degree at Aichi Gakuin University.

A scholar of linguistics and Japanology who taught Qian Lin, Itsuko Nishikawa studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Minayev studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1858–1862). He held a post at its Faculty of Oriental Studies (~1871–1890) and taught Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, Dmitry Kudryavsky, and Sergey Oldenburg.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Minaev studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber. He became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University and taught Shcherbatskoy, Oldenburg, and Kudryavsky.

A linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969), Ives Goddard held posts at Harvard University (~1969–1975) and at the Smithsonian Institution and National Museum of Natural History (~1975–2021).

Working in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Ives Waldo earned a PhD at the University of Oxford, studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988), and taught David P. Jackson.
